To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) remembered semantic analyses of text can be useful in language-endowed intelligent agent environments, 2) they are best represented in a formal metalanguage that is ontologically grounded, and 3) they are best stored in a formal knowledge representation system such as the Cyc ontology.
(1) remembered text inputs can be useful for intelligent agents, (2) these inputs can be represented in a metalanguage, and (3) they can be stored and retrieved in a database.
(1) the semantic analysis of text input is a form of memory, and (2) this memory is best recorded in a metalanguage used to represent knowledge in a specific environment.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of a language-endowed intelligent agent’s lexicon that includes all of these kinds of lexical knowledge.
the development of a computational resource that can be used to improve the language processing capabilities of intelligent agents.
the design of a computational resource that can be used in a variety of intelligent agent applications to provide a robust and efficient means of interpreting language input.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the more specific and context sensitive the interpretation of a text fragment, the more useful it will be to an intelligent agent.

a robust computational lexicon should include the following types of lexical entries: compositional expectations for argument-taking words, idiomatic entries for non-compositional words and phrases, entries that record the compositional analyses of semi-compositional expressions, and entries that record the semantic interpretations of remembered text inputs.

the most effective computational lexicon is one that includes all of these types of knowledge, and that the most effective language-endowed intelligent agent is one that can access all of these types.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have created a new type of corpus, which we call a semantic memory corpus, and which can be used by intelligent agents to enhance their language comprehension capabilities.
we have developed a framework for the annotation of text corpora that is suitable for language-endowed intelligent agents.
we are building a language-endowed intelligent agent that is capable of learning from natural language input and using that knowledge to interact with humans.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the design of robust computational lexicons must include the possibility of storing semantic interpretations of actual text inputs, and that the design of language-endowed intelligent agents must allow for the use of such lexicon elements.
a language-endowed agent can benefit from a lexicon that includes a variety of string-to-meaning mappings, including those that are not strictly compositional.
the semantic analyses of text input can be used to augment the lexicon of intelligent agents, and that the resulting lexicon can be more efficient than one based on compositional semantics.
